label: PF Backlog 652
title: Execution trail: OpenCode Go token pricing/cost + box-drawn (Cursor-style) tables

decisions.note: HIL requested OpenCode Go cost + Cursor-style tables; design sha 7ff7e891170c: 2 blockers actioned (ADR-0010 + guardrails), 5 majors actioned.
HIL requested cost + Cursor-style tables; sha 32b7bda5731b: 0 blockers, 3 majors accepted as pricing-version/freshness follow-ups.

brief.problem: Trail usage shows cost 0 because no OpenCode Go pricing is wired and tables are raw markdown.
brief.what_adds: A pricing config + cost calculation and Cursor-style box tables in the trail show.
brief.why_now: HIL needs real cost and a readable completion table per item.
brief.success: Cost reflects OpenCode Go list prices; the trail renders as proper tables.

objective: Compute review/session cost from OpenCode Go list prices and render the execution-trail stages/tests/final completion as box-drawn tables.
acceptance_criteria: config/model-pricing.json (registered; source=opencode.ai/data, unit=USD per 1M tokens) maps the review/session models (mimo-v2.6-flash: input 0.14/output 0.28/cached 0.0028; deepseek-v4.1-flash: 0.07/0.30/0.0015; deepseek-v4-flash: 0.30/1.20/0.0060) and the trail computes cost = (input-cached)*input + cached*cached_input + output*output per 1M, preferring provider-reported cost when present.

python -m core.execution_trail show --item <ID> renders the stage, test and final completion tables as box-drawn (Cursor-style) tables with wrapped cells; usage shows input/output/cached/cost and 'not captured' when a source is absent.

Tests cover the cost formula, unknown-model cost_source=unavailable, provider-reported cost precedence, box table rendering/wrapping, and the existing trail/check behavior; precheck (including the execution-trail completion gate) passes.
out_of_scope: Changing the gate order or pricing for models not in the catalog.
approach: Add config/model-pricing.json (opencode.ai/data list prices, USD/1M) and registry entry; add price_usage()/box table rendering to core/execution_trail.py; record provider cost when supplied else compute (input-cached)*input + cached*cached_input + output*output; show wraps cells in Unicode box tables; completion can attach item.execution.usage if a worker recorded it. Add tests for cost/unknown/provider-cost/box wrapping.

prior_decisions: OpenCode Data list prices (opencode.ai/data) are the pricing authority
assumptions: Cost uses (input-cached)*input + cached*cached_input + output*output per 1M; provider cost wins when present.

Tables are rendered with Unicode box drawing and wrapped cells; no external table dependency.

Extends execution_trail show/usage; no new engine.

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=7ff7e891170c
BLOCKER:
  - Language rule: `price_usage()` and box-table rendering are *new shipped logic* added to Python (`core/execution_trail.py`); AGENTS.md requires new shipped logic in Go. Either move computation/rendering to a Go surface (Python stays a thin CLI) or record an explicit ADR/exception in docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md before Gate 1.5.
  - No guardrail checklist answers in the design (CL-008): reversibility, authz/tenant scope, blast radius, invariants, observability are unstated for the new pricing/usage path; approval cannot proceed while these are PENDING.
MAJOR:
  - Formula invariant unguarded: if `cached > input` (bad/partial telemetry) the term `(input-cached)*input` yields a negative cost. State and test the invariant `0 <= cached <= input`, clamp or mark `cost_source=unavailable` on violation.
  - Provider-reported cost precedence is unchecked: a wrong-unit or wrong-currency provider value silently wins. Record `cost_source` + raw value, and log/metric the delta between reported and computed cost for drift detection.
  - Model-id normalization absent: variants like `provider/model`, `:latest`, or casing differences will fall through to `unavailable` and silently zero-out spend reporting. Define an alias/normalization strategy with tests.
  - Pricing catalog is a snapshot with no freshness signal: record `source`, `fetched_at`/version and emit an alert when upstream `opencode.ai/data` prices diverge from the registered file, else costs drift indefinitely.
  - Reuse: confirm no existing price/usage owner (Go pricing table, prior config, provider SDK cost field) is being duplicated by `config/model-pricing.json`; single source of truth must be named in the design.
MINOR:
  - Registration integrity untested: add a test that `config/model-pricing.json` validates against the store schema and that `config/store-registry.json` entry and on-disk file agree (missing/extra registration fails precheck).
  - Float precision: define display rounding (e.g., 6 dp USD) and avoid exact float equality in cost-formula tests; state rounding invariant so aggregated session cost is stable.
  - Rendering widths: wrapping must handle wide/CJK glyphs and a deterministic width source (fixed width or explicit env) so box tests aren't terminal-dependent.
  - `item.execution.usage` from workers is trusted unvalidated: validate token fields (non-negative ints, known model key) at ingest, else fall back to `not captured`.
  - Observability: emit a single structured log/metric for `cost_source=unavailable` and for render failures so silent cost gaps are diagnosable.
NIT:
  - Consider a `--json` output mode alongside box tables so downstream tooling doesn't parse ANSI/Unicode.
  - Docs note should state the pricing formula and unit (USD per 1M tokens) in docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md, not only the file path.
  - Unknown-model rendering should visually distinguish "not captured" from "$0.00" to avoid implying free usage.
SUMMARY:
  - Design is directionally right (versioned pricing config, provider-cost precedence, unknown-model honesty, box rendering with tests) but is blocked on the Go/Python language-rule placement and on missing guardrail-checklist answers (CL-008).
  - Top risks: unvalidated provider-reported cost, missing `cached <= input` invariant, model-id drift causing silent `unavailable` costs, and no freshness signal on upstream prices.
  - Recommend Gate 1.5 re-review after the language-rule decision, invariant/clamp tests, registration-validation test, and observability of unavailable costs are added.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=32b7bda5731b
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Cost evidence is not reproducible: `record()` bakes `price_usage()` output into the append-only trail, but `usage_totals()` re-runs `price_usage()` at read time, so displayed totals use the *current* catalog while stored events keep write-time costs. No pricing version/`fetched_at` snapshot is referenced per event; a catalog update silently rewrites historical totals.
  - `_pricing()` swallows every load exception into `{"models": {}, "aliases": {}}` with no logging, no trail marker, and no precheck signal — a missing/corrupt/renamed catalog makes all future events `cost_source=unavailable` with zero observability.
  - `_PRICING_CACHE` is a process-lifetime global with no invalidation; any long-lived consumer (or test run importing after a file change) sees stale prices indefinitely.
MINOR:
  - `test_show_renders_stages_tests_and_next` was weakened: `"| 1 | gate0 | pass |"` → substring `"gate0"`, losing regression coverage of ordering, status column and padding; `test_box_table_wraps_long_cells` asserts only `count("|") > 4`, not that wrapping preserves column alignment.
  - Provider-cost path skips all token validation (`negative`/`cached > input` unvalidated when `provider_cost_usd` present), and `architect_review._llm_call` accepts `cost`/`total_cost`/`cost_usd` with no unit or magnitude sanity check — a per-token or currency-mismatched value is trusted as USD.
  - Validation (`invalid_usage`) is only reachable when the model is priced; unknown-model invalid usage reports `unavailable`, masking bad telemetry.
  - `store-registry.json` allow glob `"model-pricing.json"` is bare (no path) — it allowlists any file with that basename anywhere in the tree; scope it to `product-forge/config/`.
  - No refresh/staleness mechanism or gate for the pricing snapshot (`fetched_at: 2026-10-25`); ADR-0010 defers upstream-divergence alerts to an unspecified follow-up without a backlog item reference.
  - `price_usage` overwrites `u["model"]` with the normalized name only in the computed path, changing the field's semantics for downstream consumers inconsistently.
  - `_box` `wrap()` uses `replace_whitespace=False`, so embedded newlines/tabs in summaries/commands can break row alignment; `show()` no longer truncates summaries (the old `[:160]` cap is gone), so long summaries produce very tall tables.
  - The ADR cites `config/language-rule.json` `allow_new_python` as the governance exception, but the diff contains no change to that file — verify the allowlist entry actually covers the new pricing/rendering code paths (precheck confirmation only asserted in prose).
NIT:
  - `_box` builds `top`, `sep`, `bot` as three identical strings; one constant would do.
  - Hard-coded widths (`[4,15,9,28,10,44]`, etc.) duplicate the 44-char cap logic and will silently mis-wrap if headers change.
  - `usage_totals` reads `total["cost_usd"] += ...` before the `cost_usd is None` unpriced check — works, but the ordering invites a refactor bug.
  - `price_usage` in `record()` means every writer pays catalog I/O on first call; a lazy-but-announced preload or explicit `refresh_pricing()` API would be cleaner for tooling reuse.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid, well-scoped delivery: pricing catalog with provenance, provider-cost precedence, ADR-0010 governance rationale, and tests for the core formula/precedence/normalization are all present; no blocker.
  - Top risks: (1) write-time vs read-time pricing divergence makes historical cost evidence non-reproducible and unversioned; (2) silent catalog-load failure yields permanently unpriced trails with no observability.
  - Secondary concerns: weakened show/box test assertions, unvalidated provider cost units, and an over-broad registry allow glob — address before relying on the trail as audit evidence.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
